summary.headline: Consolidated revenue rose 18% YoY to INR 20,048 crore and operating EBITDA 34% to INR 693 crore in Q1 FY27, with Edible Oil volume only 2%.
summary.overview: AWL Agri Business reported broad-based growth in Q1 FY27, with consolidated revenue up 18% YoY to INR 20,048 crore on 7% underlying volume growth. Operating EBITDA rose 34% to INR 693 crore, with PBT up 48% and PAT up 40%, which management attributed to a Food-led mix, disciplined pricing and efficiencies. Edible Oil volume grew only 2% due to channel destocking and supply chain issues amid palm oil volatility, while Industry Essentials grew volume 13%. Management said July trends had improved and reiterated FY27 segment operating guidance, and changed segment disclosure to revenue, volume growth and margin for Food and FMCG.

financial_highlights.change: +15% YoY; EBITDA per ton +33% YoY; volume +2% YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Alternate channels (modern trade, e-com, quick commerce)

segments.name: Food and FMCG
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,726 crore, up 22% YoY; segment EBITDA INR 104 crore at 6% margin. Rice grew over 40% YoY, Tops sauces/pickles/convenience food grew 23%; Madhur sugar brand added this quarter.

segments.name: Edible Oil
segments.commentary: Volume up 2% YoY due to channel destocking, supply chain disruption and sluggish trade; revenue up 15% and EBITDA per ton up 33% YoY.

segments.name: Industry Essentials
segments.commentary: Volume up 13% and revenue up 28% YoY; EBITDA up 47% YoY. Oleochemicals and specialty chemicals now over 40% of segment revenue; capacity being expanded at Southern facility.

guidance_outlook: Food and FMCG: double-digit volume and revenue growth, with revenue growth guided at 18%-20%; EBITDA margin to be judged on the average of the last four to five quarters rather than the 6% of Q1.
Food and FMCG: management also cited mid-teen revenue growth and a 3%-4% EBITDA margin range as the operating framework.
Edible Oil: volume growth of about 5%-6% for the remaining nine months of FY27; EBITDA expected at INR 4,000-4,500 per ton.
Industry Essentials: volume growth of about 8%-9%; EBITDA expected at INR 3,000-3,500 per ton.

Madhur: target to scale from about 15,000 tons/month to about 20,000 tons/month by year end; FY27 revenue from the brand estimated at INR 700-800 crore; royalty of 0.5% of sales payable to Shree Renuka Sugars.
2030 vision: revenue above INR 100,000 crore and EBITDA above INR 4,000 crore. Steady-state capex assumed at about INR 700 crore per year for modelling.

qa_highlights.question: Dhiraj Mistry (Jefferies): What revenue, growth and EBITDA margin should be expected for Food and FMCG for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided double-digit volume and revenue growth, with revenue growth of about 18%-20%; the 6% Q1 margin should not be the benchmark, and the average of the last four to five quarters is the right yardstick given the investment phase.

qa_highlights.question: Dhiraj Mistry: What revenue, margin and royalty terms apply to Madhur, and what are the targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Madhur sells about 15,000 tons/month, targeted at 20,000 tons/month by year end; FY27 revenue estimated at INR 700-800 crore; royalty 0.5% of sales to Shree Renuka Sugars; margin guidance to be in line with the overall Food segment.

qa_highlights.question: Dhiraj Mistry: What Edible Oil volume growth is expected over the medium term and full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 volume was hit by destocking, supply chain issues and sluggish trade; management is not guiding 2% and expects 5%-6% volume growth over the remaining nine months, with festive and post-monsoon demand from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Ashutosh Joytiraditya (ICICI Securities): What capex and market share gains are budgeted for the 2030 vision?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific four-year capex figure; capex will follow capacity needs, with Edible Oil refining at 60%-61% utilisation likely exhausted in a couple of years. Steady-state modelling assumption is about INR 700 crore per year.

qa_highlights.question: Ashutosh Joytiraditya: What efficiencies will the higher Wilmar ownership bring, and how much can domestic oilseed sourcing reduce imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Sourcing efficiency is unchanged; the main new lever is Wilmar's R&D and technical expertise. Management declined to give an import-reduction number, noting about 70% of edible oil requirement is imported and mustard is the focus.

qa_highlights.question: Lakshmi Narayan (Tunga Investments): What share of raw material is imported and from Wilmar, and what is the volume growth outlook? Also, B2C/B2B mix of Food?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70%+ of edible oil is imported, of which about one-third is from Wilmar; palm is about 30% of oil volumes. Blended volume growth of 8%-9% is guided. Food is more than 80% B2C and about 15% B2B.

qa_highlights.question: Lakshmi Narayan: How are Wilmar transactions priced and what are the stock days and oil mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Wilmar transactions are at arm's length, including pricing and credit period. Raw material stock is 30-35 days; oil mix is about 30% palm, 30%-35% soya, 20% sunflower and 15% local oils.

capex_capacity: Edible Oil refining capacity utilisation is running at close to 60%-61%; management expects it to be exhausted in the next couple of years, which may require capex.
Food business: about 50% of Food volume comes from contractual or tolling operations, which management wants to convert to own operations, implying significant capex.

Industry Essentials: capacity being expanded at the Southern manufacturing facility to raise the share of higher value-added specialty products (oleochemicals and specialty chemicals now over 40% of segment revenue).
No specific capex figure given for the next four years; steady-state modelling assumption of about INR 700 crore per year.
Mustard sourcing: Solidaridad and SEA programme adopting about 3,500 model mustard farms; about 18%-19% of procurement (castor seed) is bought directly from farmers.
demand_pricing: Food and FMCG revenue INR 1,726 crore, up 22% YoY; Rice up over 40% YoY; Tops sauces, pickles and convenience food up 23% YoY; Madhur added this quarter.

Edible Oil volume up 2% YoY on channel destocking after sharp global price volatility, supply chain disruption and sluggish trade; primary pipeline described as dried up; management says July has improved.
Industry Essentials volume up 13% and revenue up 28% YoY; EBITDA up 47% YoY.

Alternate channels (modern trade, e-commerce, quick commerce) up 27% YoY; quick commerce up 56% YoY. Direct reach about 970,000 outlets; Nielsen total reach 2.6 million outlets; rural presence in over 63,000 towns.
Madhur sells about 15,000 tons/month, targeted to reach about 20,000 tons/month by year end; FY27 brand revenue estimated at INR 700-800 crore; royalty 0.5% of sales to Shree Renuka Sugars.

Guidance: Food and FMCG revenue growth 18%-20%, double-digit volume growth, EBITDA margin judged on a four-to-five quarter average rather than the 6% in Q1. Edible Oil volume 5%-6% for the remaining nine months, EBITDA INR 4,000-4,500 per ton. Industry Essentials volume 8%-9%, EBITDA INR 3,000-3,500 per ton.
risks_watch: Edible Oil volume recovery: management expects 5%-6% for the remaining nine months after 2% in Q1; monitor July and Q2 festive pipeline.
Palm and edible oil price volatility, with management describing volatility as the new normal; imports are about 70% of edible oil requirement.
Food margin: Q1 EBITDA margin of 6% versus the 3%-4% framework; investment-phase spending on brands, distribution and Madhur.
Madhur execution: scaling from about 15,000 to 20,000 tons/month by year end; 0.5% royalty to Shree Renuka Sugars and brand remains licensed.
Capex timing: Edible Oil utilisation near 60%-61% and Food tolling conversion may need capex beyond the INR 700 crore per year steady-state assumption.
Related-party exposure: about one-third of imported edible oil is sourced from Wilmar, on arm's length terms per management.
key_quotes: Revenue grew by 18% year-on-year to INR (+20,000) crore and the quality of our earning continues to improve alongside this growth.
Our integrated sourcing capabilities, pricing discipline and premiumization initiative enabled us to effectively navigate this environment while sustaining our market leadership.
So, 6% may not be the guidance, of course. The average of last four quarters or five quarters should be something which we should be consistently delivering.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Food, Industry Essentials and channel growth, but cautious and somewhat defensive on Edible Oil volumes, citing destocking and volatility. Management was evasive on capex quantum and import-reduction numbers, offering only directional answers.
